indian.headline: Sensex and Nifty rose on IT strength, but FPI selling pressure persists into October.
indian.lead: Sensex and Nifty rose on IT strength, but FPI selling pressure persists into October.
indian.brief: Sensex gained 0.56% and Nifty 50 climbed 0.65%, with IT stocks leading the charge as the market recovered from early weakness.
why: IT sector surged 3.9%, driven by stocks like TechM jumping 7%, lifting index heavyweights and offsetting weakness in defensive sectors.
FPIs continued heavy selling (₹44,166 cr withdrawn in October alone), yet domestic buying and improved sentiment capped downside losses.
Banking sector gained only 0.06% despite recovery hopes, as Yes Bank's AT-1 bond ruling and broader FPI outflows tempered financial stock enthusiasm.
Realty and FMCG fell (down 0.3% and 0.4%), showing investors rotated out of defensive names into cyclicals like IT and metals.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities opened under pressure from relentless foreign investor withdrawals but staged a recovery through the session. Sensex rose 250 points to close 0.56% higher while Nifty 50 added 0.65%, with the IT index powering ahead 3.9% on optimism around global tech demand. TechM led the charge, climbing 7%, a rare bright spot in a market grappling with ₹44,166 crore in FPI outflows already this month—part of a larger 2026 withdrawal wave exceeding ₹3 lakh crore.

The day revealed an internal tug-of-war: cyclical sectors like IT and metals (up 1.0%) attracted risk-on buyers, while defensive plays including Realty, FMCG, and Pharma slipped into negative territory. Banking gained a meager 0.06%, weighed down by the Supreme Court's ruling on Yes Bank's 2020 AT-1 bond write-off, though S&P said ratings would hold. Meanwhile, Reliance's bold Jio IPO decision and Sebi's bond and trading rule tweaks signaled regulatory support, yet failed to offset the headwind of sustained foreign selling. The market closed modestly positive but fragile.

us.headline: US markets closed higher despite tech weakness; financials and healthcare led the rally.
us.lead: US markets closed higher despite tech weakness; financials and healthcare led the rally.
us.brief: S&P 500 gained 0.33%, Nasdaq edged up 0.08%, and Dow jumped 1.08% on October 16.
why: Financials surged 1.4% after Morgan Stanley beat earnings expectations with strong equities trading revenue, offsetting Bank of America's profit decline and regulatory penalties.
Healthcare advanced 1.9%, providing steady support while tech sector fell 0.7% and energy dropped 1.6%, creating a defensive tilt.
Mixed banking earnings—Morgan Stanley's trading beat versus Bank of America's miss and software remediation costs—showed uneven strength in the sector.
us.narrative:
US stock markets ended October 16 in positive territory as selective strength in financials and healthcare offset weakness in tech and energy. The Dow led with a 1.08% gain, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted more modest advances. Morgan Stanley's Q3 results impressed investors with trading revenue beating expectations by $909 million, but Bank of America's 17% profit decline and $1.2 billion regulatory penalty tempered enthusiasm. Bank of America also revealed it deployed 3,000 internal staff and 1,000 contractors to fix software flaws, indicating ongoing tech challenges in the sector.

Globally, Indian IT stocks showed strength—Wipro rose 5% and Tech Mahindra jumped 7% after quarterly results—while South Korean markets rebounded 2.36% after a severe Thursday plunge, though headed for their worst week since 2008. In consumer news, KFC announced a historic beverage switch to Coca-Cola in US restaurants after 40 years with PepsiCo. The mixed signals—strong trading profits alongside regulatory pressures and software costs—underscore the complex backdrop for risk assets heading into earnings season.

tiles.sub: Trading revenue exceeded expectations by $909 million; Q3 profit $4.91 billion.
